channel.title: The Peptides4Pets Journal
channel.description: Evidence-first writing on peptides, supplements and longevity science for dogs and cats — graded honestly, cited properly.

item.title: My 14-Year-Old Dog Started Running Again: An Honest Owner's Account of BPC-157 + TB-500
item.description: This is the one thing the rest of this site does not have: a personal account. One old dog, two years, and a change I did not expect — told as an anecdote, not as proof, and held against what the research does and does not show.

item.title: BPC-157 South Africa: A Pet Owner's Guide to Availability, Regulation and Evidence
item.description: BPC-157 searches in South Africa usually end at grey-market sellers, import delays or confusing SAHPRA status. Here is what local pet owners actually need to know.

item.title: Calming Peptides: The Milk Protein With Placebo-Controlled Trials
item.description: A milk-derived peptide with placebo-controlled trials in both cats and dogs — vet visits, anxiety disorders, stress physiology. The quiet overachiever of pet calming science.

item.title: The Science of Pet Longevity: Dog Aging Project, Loyal, and What's Coming
item.description: For the first time in history, pet aging is being studied like the medical condition it is. The biggest trials ever run in dogs are underway — here is what they are testing and what it means for yours.

item.title: KPV for Dog Gut and Skin: Reading the Preclinical Evidence
item.description: Three amino acids, one elegant anti-inflammatory pathway, and a stack of mouse studies. KPV is genuinely interesting gut science — here is what would still need to be proven for dogs.

item.title: TB-500 and Dogs: Promise vs Proof
item.description: Thymosin beta-4 has a real regenerative biology — and TB-500 borrows its reputation. Racing regulators banned it years ago. Here is what that signal does and does not mean for your dog.

item.title: Collagen Peptides for Dog Joints: The Strongest Evidence in Pet Nutrition
item.description: A placebo-controlled force-plate trial, a head-to-head against a registered NSAID, and a cartilage biomarker study. Collagen is the one joint supplement with real canine RCTs — here is what they found.

item.title: BPC-157 for Dogs: What the Science Actually Says (2026)
item.description: One real canine pharmacokinetic study, a large rodent literature, and zero canine efficacy trials. Here is what BPC-157 can — and cannot — claim for dogs.
